difficultyReason: Strengthen by ruling out an alternative explanation (instrument insensitivity). Trap (D) sounds like it supports 'current theory' and might seem to strengthen; trap (E) offers a tangential fact about neutron-star origins.
stimulus: The supernova event of 1987 is interesting in that there is still no evidence of the neutron star that current theory says should have remained after a supernova of that size. This is in spite of the fact that many of the most sensitive instruments ever developed have searched for the tell-tale pulse of radiation that neutron stars emit. Thus, current theory is wrong in claiming that supernovas of a certain size always produce neutron stars.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Most supernova remnants that astronomers have detected have a neutron star nearby.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sensitive astronomical instruments have detected neutron stars much farther away than the location of the 1987 supernova.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The supernova of 1987 was the first that scientists were able to observe in progress.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Several important features of the 1987 supernova are correctly predicted by the current theory.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some neutron stars are known to have come into existence by a cause other than a supernova explosion.

explanations.correct: The argument assumes that if a neutron star existed at the supernova site, our instruments would have detected it. Showing that our instruments have detected neutron stars much farther away than this site directly bolsters that assumption and so strengthens the no-neutron-star-must-exist conclusion.
explanations.A: Consistent with the theory being right most of the time — does not strengthen the claim that this particular case refutes the theory.
explanations.C: Irrelevant — observation history doesn't speak to whether a neutron star exists now.
explanations.D: Weakens, if anything — the theory has predictive track record here.
explanations.E: Tangential; the question is about this supernova producing a neutron star, not other origins.
